limits: Needs the network; exact matches only.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which published iGEM part carries exactly these bases?

description: Identify a stretch of DNA by asking the iGEM Registry which published part carries exactly those bases, and hand back that part's own description, Sequence-Ontology role, literature citation and license. The match is decided by comparing bases, never by a name — so a pipeline can label a fragment it has assembled, or check that a feature really is the part it is called.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cap.description: most candidate sequences to fetch and compare before stopping and saying so.

name.description: a name to narrow the candidates by (a feature name, or a part id like BBa_R0040). It only narrows: the bases decide the match. Leave it empty to compare every candidate of this exact length, which is slower and can be far more requests.

sequence.description: the bases to identify — a feature’s span, an assembled fragment, a pasted oligo.

name: match_part_by_sequence

coverage.description: what was and was not compared: the population at this length, the candidates the narrowing produced, how many were read back, and whether the cap stopped it. A null answer is only as strong as this.

description.description: the registry’s own prose — the half a coordinate cannot tell you

licence.description: the SPDX identifier the registry states for that part

matched.description: whether any compared part carries these exact bases

matches.description: every part that carries these bases — several may, and the registry keeps them apart

page.description: the registry page, so the claim can be checked without us

part.description: the best match’s registry id, exact before reverse-complement

role.description: its Sequence-Ontology role, as the registry files it

strand.description: `exact` when the bases agree as given, `reverse-complement` when they agree flipped

title.description: the registry’s own short title for that part
